text:
maria: Quick question — Terraform creates an ExternalSecret in namespace `infra` named `app-secrets`. Our Helm release deploys into `app` namespace. I tried to `envFrom` that secret but the pod spec ends up invalid / chart blows up when secret is missing. Is there a clean Helm pattern to check for a secret and only render `envFrom` if it exists, or should we change the infra?

kevin: you can use Helm's `lookup` to see if a Secret exists and conditionally render. e.g.:
```yaml
{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" "infra" "app-secrets" }}
{{- if $s.metadata.name }}
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ $s.metadata.name | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
Note: `lookup` talks to the cluster, so `helm template` without cluster access won't see it. Also include `quote`/`| trim` to be safe.

ali: caution — Kubernetes will reject cross-namespace secretRefs. You cannot mount a Secret from namespace `infra` into a Pod in `app` namespace by referencing it in `envFrom`. That pattern is invalid at the API level. Two safe options: have ExternalSecret create/sync the Secret into the target namespace (`app`), or have Terraform/ExternalSecret write the secret into `app` namespace as well.

maria: ah damn, that explains the validation errors. I assumed secret refs could point across namespaces. If we sync the secret into `app` namespace then the lookup approach works?

kevin: yeah. If the controller copies/syncs it into `app`, then `lookup "v1" "Secret" "app" "app-secrets"` will work. If you want to be robust and keep templating simple, you can also render env keys with `optional: true` so missing secrets don't kill the pod. Example for a single key:
```yaml
env:
- name: EXTERNAL_API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: {{ .Values.env.secretName | quote }}
      key: api_key
      optional: true
```
`optional: true` prevents a crash if the key/secret is missing at runtime.

jonathan: another pattern that's safe for chart authors who want to avoid conditional indentation pain: build the whole block in a helper and `toYaml` it with `nindent`. e.g.:
```yaml
{{- define "myapp.envFromIfSecret" -}}
{{- if .Values.env.secretName }}
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ .Values.env.secretName | quote }}
{{- end -}}
{{- end }}

# usage in deployment template
{{- include "myapp.envFromIfSecret" . | nindent 8 }}
```
That way you don't end up with stray `envFrom:` with no items.

helm-bot: extra checklist: :clipboard:
- Remember cross-namespace secretRefs are not allowed — secrets must live in the same namespace as the Pod.
- `lookup` requires cluster access and will return an object you should check with `if $s.metadata.name` (empty maps can be tricky).
- Consider making secrets optional in your Pod spec (`optional: true`) when it's safe to run without them.
- For CI/dry-run, prefer a values-driven fallback like `.Values.env.secretName` so templates don't depend on cluster state.

maria: thanks — plan is to update ExternalSecret to sync into `app` namespace, add a `.Values.env.secretName` fallback, and use the helper + `nindent` pattern. Will open a PR for the chart and the ExternalSecret change in infra. cc @kevin @ali for review. :thumbsup:

kevin: lgtm. If you want I can add a little unit test with `helm template` and a fake values file to ensure both cases (secret present vs absent) render cleanly.

ali: and I'll update the ExternalSecret TF module to allow `targetNamespace` param so teams can opt to sync.

maria: awesome — thanks all. I'll link the PRs here when I have them.
